Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short comparison and a recommended path below; looping Karthik (solutions architect) for technical detail and a diagram (attached).

Executive summary
- PrivateLink: best when you need strong network isolation and minimal routing changes on customer side. Easier to enforce per-service access and avoids full VPC routing overlap. Slightly higher egress cost and more configuration for endpoint services.
- VPC peering: lowest intra-VPC latency and cost-effective for high-throughput internal traffic, but requires overlapping CIDR planning, and cross-account peering may increase blast radius and routing complexity.
- Site-to-site VPN: fastest to stand up for proof-of-concept; tolerates on-prem NAT and simple firewall rules, but not ideal for sustained production inference due to latency/jitter and management complexity at scale.

Our recommendation for Optima (us-west-2, two colo sites): PrivateLink for production inference (security + stable peering at the service level) + a short-lived VPN for initial onboarding/testing and tooling (CI, file sync). If Optima prioritizes absolute per-token cost and can coordinate CIDR and route tables across accounts, VPC peering is an alternative for strictly internal deployments.

Attached: optima_network_options_v1.png (high-level diagram), redwood_sow_draft_optima.pdf (SOW skeleton).

2) If Optima wants PrivateLink: we can provide an endpoint service ARN and a short runbook for your networking team.
3) For procurement: Marissa will follow-up with SOW and pricing options.

Sam — adding technical context and a short ops checklist. TL;DR: PrivateLink for production; VPN for onboarding; peering only if Optima can commit to CIDR coordination and cross-account route controls.

Tradeoffs (concise)
- PrivateLink (AWS NLB-based interface endpoints)
  - Pros: minimal customer-side routing changes, no cross-account route propagation, supports VPCs and on-prem access via Direct Connect/Transit, avoids exposing Redwood subnets. Good for strict network isolation/compliance.
  - Cons: per-GB data processing/endpoint costs; if you need very high sustained throughput (multi-Gbps) consider NLB sizing and regional scaling. Also TLS termination and mutual TLS options must be agreed for egress path.

- VPC Peering
  - Pros: flat L3 connectivity, lowest latency, works well for predictable high-throughput workloads, no per-endpoint charges.
  - Cons: must ensure non-overlapping CIDRs, cross-account route table maintenance, potential for broader lateral movement unless strict security groups/AWS NACLs enforced. Not available across regions.

- Site-to-site VPN
  - Pros: quick setup, supports on-prem colo without changing cloud routing.
  - Cons: jitter and latency variability, potential bandwidth limits depending on vendor appliances, higher operational overhead (rekeys, monitoring). Not recommended as sole production path for latency-sensitive LLM inference.

Operational checklist (PrivateLink)
- Provide account ID(s) + VPC IDs for endpoint attachment or Direct Connect routing details.
- Confirm allowed CIDR ranges for endpoint ENIs; avoid overlapping with Optima subnets used at colos.
- Open ports: 443 (TLS) for API, health-check ports (we'll provide list), and management ports for monitoring if you require agent-based telemetry.
- mTLS requirement: if Optima requires client certs, we'll enable mutual TLS and provide cert thumbprint guidance.
- Perf verification: run 1-hour steady-state token-generation tests from both colos; measure p95 latency and tail jitter before migrating traffic.

Attachment: I added a diagram overlaying PrivateLink + short-lived VPN for onboarding in optima_network_options_v1.png.

- Pricing note: PrivateLink data processing will appear on the monthly usage; we'll estimate based on expected tokens/s but can provide a not-to-exceed on a per-month proposal for the initial 3 months.

Next steps: If you confirm approach (PrivateLink + transient VPN), I will:

Two small asks before kickoff:
- Can you include the expected ENI IP ranges so our firewall team can pre-approve rules?
- For the performance test, we'll run from our two colo sites (sjc1 and pdx1). Can you provide the perf test script/traffic profile (tokens/sec target) you want us to use?

I'll be out Thursday morning but otherwise available for a 30-minute kickoff on Friday afternoon.
